page: Microsoft Azure B2ps_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bpsv2 family, built on the arm64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and lacks local storage or integrated GPUs. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports Premium Storage for external disk attachments.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile that is generally constrained. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is average at 1822.08, and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 24.19 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded operations show limitations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3597.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2025.0, both falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 140.71 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 26.73 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and lower-tier performance in database operations and static web serving, this server is positioned for low-intensity workloads. It is suitable for development environments, light testing, or small background tasks that experience intermittent usage. The ARM-based architecture and burstable resource model provide a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained high CPU utilization, trading off raw computational speed and memory throughput for resource density.
